questions.history: Start present and empty, override with `temporary`, then return normally.
questions.prediction: Both callbacks see `temporary`. The PR reports `default` afterward on the parent. The merge should return `""` afterward.
questions.basis: The default argument distinguishes absence from an intentionally empty value. The landed test checks an empty value after scope exit.
questions.refutation: The merge returns `default`, retains `temporary`, or never exposes the override.

questions.history: Repeat with an initially absent property and with the initial value `original`.
questions.prediction: On both revisions the final reads should be `default` and `original`, respectively.
questions.basis: The two distinct initial states are recorded before entering the same scope.
questions.refutation: The formerly absent key remains present or the original nonempty value changes.

questions.history: Keep the initially empty key and nest a second override with value `inner`. Throw a sentinel `RuntimeException` from the inner Runnable and catch it inside the outer callback.
questions.prediction: On the merge the reader should see `inner`, then `temporary` after the catch, then `""` outside both scopes. The caught exception should be the sentinel.
questions.basis: Each nested scope has its own entry state. Exception unwinding exercises the same restoration obligation before the outer callback continues.
questions.refutation: Either scope leaks its override or the caller receives a different exception.
